name: Arizona State University minimum stipend for graduate assistants and Graduate Assistant Handbook
covers: Graduate Teaching Assistants/Associates (TA) and Research Assistants/Associates (RA); Graduate Service Assistants (GSA) receive no tuition award or health insurance
note: The provost sets the minimum stipend; the Graduate College page restates it for a 50% academic-year RA/TA appointment. Stipends are paid bi-weekly through payroll and may vary by unit and duties above the minimum. Assistants may work at most 50% FTE (20 hours a week) in fall and spring.

name: Agreement between Trustees of Boston University and Boston University Graduate Workers Union (BUGWU), SEIU Local 509
union: Boston University Graduate Workers Union (BUGWU), SEIU Local 509
covers: Graduate student employees enrolled in BU graduate programs who are paid to provide research, instructional, or teaching services (titles include Graduate Research Fellow, Graduate Teaching Fellow, Grader, Graduate Assistant, Graduate Grader, Group Tutor, Laboratory Assistant, Research Assistant, Teaching Assistant, and Tutor); non-service fellows are excluded.
note: The agreement runs from ratification; the Provost's office dates ratification October 16, 2024. The University signatories' DocuSign stamps on PDF pages 48-49 are dated December 5-11, 2024, but the union signatures carry no legible date, so no signing date is given here.

name: Graduate School of Arts & Sciences (GRS) five-year PhD fellowship funding
covers: PhD students in the Graduate School of Arts & Sciences, for up to five years from matriculation

name: Boston University PhD full funding model
covers: PhD students in good standing on the Charles River Campus, for five years; a separate full-funding model covers PhD students in Graduate Medical Sciences and the School of Public Health on the Medical Campus
note: The University-wide statement of PhD support. Its stipend minimums, printed through 2024-25, were overtaken by the contract's $45,000 minimum from November 15, 2024; the tuition, fee and health insurance coverage it describes is not in the contract.

name: Collective Bargaining Agreement between Brown University and the Graduate Labor Organization
union: Graduate Labor Organization (GLO)
covers: Graduate Student Employees: Ph.D. students serving as Teaching Assistants, Teaching Fellows, Research Assistants and Proctors, and Master's students serving as Teaching Assistants, Research Assistants and Proctors, during semester-length appointments, plus Master's students working at least 20 hours a week as Research Assistants (side letter). Students on fellowship without a service requirement, and students paid hourly, are excluded.
note: Made December 18, 2023 (signature dates December 18-21, 2023); terms run from July 1, 2023 and the FY24 stipend is retroactive to that date. The term ended June 30, 2026 (Brown Daily Herald, July 3, 2026). As of October 15, 2026, no successor agreement had been announced: Brown and GLO were still bargaining a 2026-2029 contract, and the union's newest bargaining update was dated July 2, 2026. The expired terms still apply: the union's June 26, 2026 post says federal labor law requires Brown to keep the status quo while bargaining continues.

name: Brown University Graduate School doctoral funding guarantee
covers: Incoming doctoral students, for five years (six in the Humanities and Social Sciences)
note: The Graduate School's published guarantee, which covers summers, tuition, the health-services fee and health and dental insurance; the GLO contract sets stipends but has no summer or tuition provision. Support may come as a teaching or research assistantship, fellowship or proctorship.

name: Collective Bargaining Agreement between Columbia University in the City of New York and Student Workers of Columbia, UAW (SWC-UAW Local 2710)
union: Student Workers of Columbia, UAW, and its Local Union, SWC-UAW Local 2710
covers: Student Employees (enrolled students who hold teaching or research appointments, such as Teaching Assistants, Teaching Fellows, Preceptors, Readers, Graduate Research Assistants and Department Research Assistants) in the bargaining unit certified by the National Labor Relations Board in Case No. 02-RC-143012
note: Dates are from the cover page; Article 32 (p. 30) runs the term from ratification through June 30, 2025. Ended by its terms on 2025-06-30. As of 2026-10-15 no successor had been reached; the University reported its twenty-first bargaining session on September 30, 2026, saying the parties "remain far apart on virtually all major elements of a labor contract".

name: Columbia University minimum PhD student support rates, set by the University after the SWC-UAW agreement expired
covers: PhD students in guaranteed years of support, both on and off teaching or research appointments, as the University's notices describe them
note: No contract sets pay in this period. The SWC-UAW agreement ended on 2025-06-30; the compensation page says it "expired on June 30, 2025, before an agreement on a successor contract could be reached", and the University's report of September 30, 2026 describes bargaining still under way. The University applied a 3% increase to minimum support pro rata from 2025-10-16 and, per the compensation page, a further 3% effective 2026-09-01. The 2025 notice gives percentages only; the dollar minimums for 2026-27 are on the compensation page (source student-benefits-compensation).

name: Collective Bargaining Agreement between Cornell University and CGSU-UE (UE Local 300)
union: Cornell Graduate Students United (CGSU-UE), UE Local 300 of the United Electrical, Radio and Machine Workers of America
covers: Graduate students enrolled in Cornell PhD and Master's degree programs at the Ithaca, Cornell Tech (Roosevelt Island) and Geneva campuses who receive a stipend from the University to provide teaching or research services, in titles including teaching assistants, research assistants, graduate assistants, and graduate research assistants. Excluded: undergraduates, graduate teaching research specialists (GTRS), fellows, DVM, MD and JD students, students at all other campuses (Doha, Washington, D.C., Rome and others), non-degree students, and the other groups listed in Article 2.
note: Article 33 makes the agreement effective upon ratification and keeps it in force up to and including May 1, 2027; Article 1 says it is entered into April 11, 2025, and the University announced ratification the same day. No signature dates appear in the PDF. Two searches (October 2026) found no successor agreement or announced successor bargaining; Article 33 lets either party open negotiations within 90 days before termination.

name: Cornell University Graduate School assistantship stipend rates (Board of Trustees minimum stipend)
covers: Graduate students on TA, GA, RA and GRA assistantships (the pages also list University Fellowship rates, which are not recorded here), with a separate table for Cornell Tech.
note: The Graduate School publishes one table per academic year. The 2023-24 and 2024-25 rates predate the CGSU-UE agreement (ratified April 11, 2025). From 2025-26 the page's 12-month assistantship figures follow Article 25 of the agreement, except that the 2026-27 figure is $48,912 here and $48,911 in the contract; both are recorded. The 9-month and summer figures are the Graduate School's; the contract only says partial appointments receive a pro rata share of the 12-month minimum. Where the Graduate School's figure equals the contract's, the contract figure is given.

name: CUNY and PSC-CUNY collective bargaining agreement, 2017-2023
union: Professional Staff Congress/CUNY (AFT Local 2334)
covers: The PSC-CUNY instructional staff unit, including Graduate Assistants A, B, C and D
note: Superseded by the 2023-2027 Memorandum of Agreement, which keeps its terms except where modified, so its non-pay provisions (workload, tuition, health insurance) still apply.

name: CUNY and PSC-CUNY Memorandum of Agreement, 2023-2027 (modifying the 2017-2023 agreement)
union: Professional Staff Congress/CUNY (AFT Local 2334)
covers: The PSC-CUNY instructional staff unit, including Graduate Assistants A, B, C and D
note: Effective on the later of membership ratification and approval by CUNY's Board of Trustees; members' ratification was announced January 14, 2025, and wage increases were paid retroactively. There is no consolidated 2023-2027 contract text. The signing date is read from the handwritten dates beside both signatures on PDF page 33 of the memorandum (12/16/2024 for CUNY, 12/16/24 for PSC-CUNY); the scan's text layer does not reproduce them.

name: CUNY Graduate Center fellowships and tuition remission (Graduate Center Fellowship, Provost's Enhancement Fellowship, Science Fellowship, CUNY Science Scholarship)
covers: Doctoral students at the Graduate Center offered five-year fellowships on admission, and doctoral students holding Graduate Assistant or adjunct titles
note: Graduate Center policy, not part of the PSC-CUNY contract. The fellowships pay a Graduate Assistant B salary under the contract's schedule plus a financial aid fellowship, so their totals follow the contract's raises.

name: Duke University and Duke University Graduate Students Union/SEIU, Southern Region collective bargaining agreement
union: Duke University Graduate Students Union/Service Employees International Union, Southern Region (Southern Region Workers United, A/W SEIU)
covers: All PhD students in Duke University departments housed at its campuses in Durham and Beaufort, North Carolina, working toward Duke Graduate School PhD degrees and employed to provide instructional or research services
note: The cover dates the agreement August 30, 2025 through March 31, 2028; Article 46 makes it effective upon ratification, and the union's ratification page says members' voting closed on August 30, 2025 with 99% in favor, so the cover's start date is the day ratification closed. The preamble says the agreement was entered into on September 25, 2025; no signature dates are given. Addendum B lets the Union extend the agreement by one year if the NLRB declines jurisdiction over the unit.

name: Duke Graduate School recommended Ph.D. stipends (before the DGSU agreement)
covers: Ph.D. students in programs housed in Trinity, Nicholas, Pratt, Nursing, Medicine, and Sanford (all position types)
note: The Graduate School's published schedule of recommended stipends before the first contract. The 2025 version says to use the 2024-25 rate until Ph.D. collective bargaining has been completed; from August 1, 2025 the Article 24 minimum applies.

name: Georgia Tech policy on Stipends for Graduate Assistantships
covers: Graduate research assistants (GRAs) and teaching assistants (GTAs) in all degree-seeking programs
note: The policy has been in effect since August 2015 and is revised each year with the next academic year's minimums; the current version (last revised June 2026) sets the 2026-27 minimums. Academic units set their own stipend levels at or above the Institute minimum and are asked to publish them. No union contract covers Georgia Tech's graduate assistants.

name: George Mason University minimum pay rates for graduate assistantships and Graduate Student Hiring Rules and Procedures
covers: Master's and doctoral graduate professional, research, and teaching assistantships paid from state or research accounts
note: The Graduate Division republishes the minimums each academic year; the current page lists AY 2026-2027. Hiring units may pay more, and stipend levels have no caps.

name: Collective Bargaining Agreement between Harvard University and the Harvard Graduate Students Union-UAW Local 5118 (2021-2025)
union: Harvard Graduate Students Union-UAW Local 5118 (HGSU-UAW), International Union, UAW
covers: Students enrolled in Harvard degree programs employed by Harvard who provide instructional services (graduate and undergraduate Teaching Fellows: teaching assistants, teaching fellows, course assistants), and students enrolled in Harvard degree programs other than Harvard College undergraduates who serve as Research Assistants, regardless of funding source, across GSAS, HBS, DCE, GSD, HGSE, SEAS, HKS, HLS, HDS, HMS, the Chan School of Public Health, and Harvard College. Excluded: undergraduates serving as research assistants, and guards and supervisors.
note: Article 36 runs the agreement from November 27, 2021 through June 30, 2025, then continues it in effect until terminated or modified on notice (at least 90 days, and no earlier than June 30, 2025). Successor bargaining began in March 2025 and no successor agreement had been reached by October 9, 2026 (see history). Status is expired-continuing because Harvard's 2026 bargaining pages still call it 'the current contract' and give its FY25 rates and $21.00 hourly minimum as the rates now paid. The signature block in this copy is blank, so no signing date is recorded. The pay rates in Article 20 for FY22 took effect July 1, 2021, before the agreement's start date. Harvard's bargaining page refers to an earlier HGSU-UAW contract ratified in 2020.

name: Harvard Griffin GSAS PhD financial support package
covers: PhD students in Harvard Kenneth C. Griffin Graduate School of Arts and Sciences programs who benefit from the GSAS financial support package (set out in each student's Notice of Financial Support)
note: Living-expense support combines stipends with Teaching Fellow and Research Assistant pay, which the HGSU-UAW agreement governs; this entry records the GSAS funding policy, not a contract. GSAS's pages give no current GSAS-wide stipend figure: the latest is the 2024-25 floor announced in December 2023. The Biophysics program page says 2026-27 rates will be determined as part of the GSAS and Graduate Student Union contract negotiations.

name: Agreement between Johns Hopkins University and TRU-UE Local 197
union: Teachers and Researchers United, United Electrical, Radio and Machine Workers of America (TRU-UE) Local 197
covers: All graduate students enrolled in University PhD programs who are employed to provide instructional or research services, including teaching assistants, research assistants, and fellows; excluding undergraduate and non-degree-seeking graduate students, postdoctoral fellows, students who receive no compensation, wages, or paid healthcare benefits from the University, students with full-time faculty or staff appointments, office clericals, managers, guards, and supervisors.
note: First contract. The cover dates it March 29, 2024 - June 30, 2027 and Article 1 says it was entered into on March 29, 2024, but Article 29 makes it effective from the date of ratification. The JHU Hub says terms were reached on March 29, and the Office of the Provost says the PhD students voted to ratify it on April 17, 2024, so the cover date, used here as the start date as the cover gives it, is the tentative-agreement date. It runs until 11:59 p.m. on June 30, 2027 and renews for twelve months at a time unless either party gives written notice at least 90 days before the expiration date or an anniversary. The signature lines are blank, and no signing date is given. Two web searches on 2026-10-13 found no successor agreement or announced successor bargaining.

name: Collective Bargaining Agreement between the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and the MIT Graduate Student Union (UE Local 256)
union: MIT Graduate Student Union, UE Local 256 (United Electrical, Radio and Machine Workers of America)
covers: Graduate students enrolled in MIT degree programs who are employed to provide instructional or research services, including research assistants, teaching assistants, and instructor Gs. Excluded: undergraduates, graduate resident advisors, graduate fellows who are not also RAs or TAs, hourly positions (graders, tutors and similar), non-degree and visiting students, and the other groups listed in Article 2.
note: Article 28 makes the agreement effective upon ratification and keeps it in force until 11:59:59 PM, May 31, 2026, then for successive one-year periods unless a party gives written notice of termination at least 60 days before expiry or the agreement is extended by mutual written agreement. The start date is the date the agreement gives for itself (Article 1, page 7: 'This Agreement is entered into as of September 23, 2023'). The union reports ratification by September 22, 2023, the union's signature block is dated February 28, 2024, and the Appendix 1 wage schedule took effect June 1, 2023, before any of those dates. Status is expired-continuing: MIT's June 4, 2026 letter says the agreement 'has now expired, as of May 31' while most of its terms remain in effect until a new contract is signed, and MIT's October 7, 2026 bargaining update shows talks on a successor still under way (see history). No successor agreement exists as of that update.

name: NC State Graduate Student Support Plan (GSSP)
covers: Graduate students on a qualifying Teaching, Research, Teaching/Research, or Extension Assistantship, or a primary fellowship, enrolled full time in an on-campus master's or doctoral program
note: No contract sets pay at NC State: N.C.G.S. 95-98 declares any contract between a State institution and a labor union acting as bargaining agent for public employees void. The GSSP minimum stipends are eligibility thresholds for the plan's tuition and health insurance benefits, not a universal pay floor: departments set actual GA stipends, and an assistantship below the threshold is allowed but carries no GSSP benefits. The only stated pay floor is the North Carolina minimum wage. The GSSP pages are undated; year-by-year minimums come from the Graduate School's GA stipend calculator and its archived versions.

name: NJIT and UCAN GSRE Memorandum of Agreement, July 1, 2022 - June 30, 2026
union: United Council of Academics at NJIT (UCAN), Rutgers Council of AAUP Chapters, AAUP-AFT, AFL-CIO
covers: Graduate Student and Research Employee (GSRE) unit. Graduate Student Employees are full-time PhD students paid a stipend as Graduate Student Teaching Assistants (including Graduate Student Assistants and University-paid Teaching Fellows), Research Assistants, or Research Assistant/Teaching Assistants; the unit also includes postdoctoral and other Research Employees, whose rates are not extracted here.
note: The memorandum amends the 2015-2019 agreement (as extended through June 30, 2022 by the December 2021 memorandum); all language it does not change continues. Pay is retroactive to July 1, 2022 for unit members employed on December 15, 2023. Retroactive 2022-23 pay was $4,323.08 for academic-year and $5,603.30 for calendar-year appointments, paid February 16, 2024; the back-pay amounts are not listed as pay rates. Members ratified the memorandum in a vote ending January 30, 2024 (NJIT's Human Resources page dates the ratification January 31). The term ended June 30, 2026; as of 2026-10-13 UCAN and NJIT were negotiating a July 1, 2026 - June 30, 2030 successor and no successor agreement was found. The contract is treated as still in force because of UCAN's statement that under New Jersey law a contract's terms continue after expiration until modified; that statement sits under a 2022 heading on the union's contracts page, which in its current version also says the contract has expired. No source states a 2026-27 stipend: the memorandum's tables end at 2025-26, and NJIT's Graduate Studies page (retrieved October 14, 2026) still lists 2025-26 as its latest year. Under the status-quo statement the 2025-26 minimums would presumably continue, but no 2026-27 figure is listed.

name: NJIT and UCAN GSRE Memorandum of Agreement, July 1, 2019 - June 30, 2022
union: United Council of Academics at NJIT (UCAN), Rutgers Council of AAUP Chapters, AAUP-AFT, AFL-CIO
covers: Graduate Student and Research Employee (GSRE) unit
note: Re-certifies the 2015-2019 agreement as a July 1, 2015 - June 30, 2022 contract with the changes listed. Covers the whole 2019-2022 term, including the years the June 2020 and March 2021 memoranda had settled. Superseded by the 2022-2026 memorandum.

name: NJIT and UCAN GSRE Memorandum of Agreement, one-year extension for July 1, 2020 - June 30, 2021
union: United Council of Academics at NJIT (UCAN), Rutgers Council of AAUP Chapters, AAUP-AFT, AFL-CIO
covers: Graduate Student and Research Employee (GSRE) unit
note: Made in March 2021; the day is uncertain in the scan, which appears to read the 25th in its opening line and the 12th in its execution line. Extends the expired contract one year while negotiations continued, freezing stipend minimums. Superseded by the December 2021 memorandum covering 2019-2022.

name: NJIT and UCAN Grad Employees Memorandum of Agreement, July 1, 2019 - June 30, 2020
union: United Council of Academics at NJIT (UCAN), Rutgers Council of AAUP Chapters, AAUP-AFT, AFL-CIO
covers: Graduate Student and Research Employee (GSRE) unit
note: The memorandum's opening line says it was 'made this 15th day of June, 2020'; its signature blocks are dated June 11 (UCAN) and June 15, 2020 (NJIT), but the copy found has no NJIT signatures, so no signing date is given. Superseded by the December 2021 memorandum covering 2019-2022.

name: Agreement between NJIT and UCAN, Graduate Student and Research Employee Bargaining Unit
union: United Council of Academics at NJIT (UCAN), Rutgers Council of AAUP Chapters, AAUP-AFT, AFL-CIO
covers: Graduate Student Assistants, Graduate Student Teaching Assistants, Graduate Student Research Assistants, University-paid (non-grant funded) full-time Teaching Fellows, Postdoctoral Research Associates, Research Associates, and Research Architects/Engineers/Scientists
note: Its unamended language carries forward through the 2019-2022 and 2022-2026 memoranda.

name: Collective Bargaining Agreement between Northwestern University and UE Local 1122 (NUGW-UE)
union: Northwestern University Graduate Workers, United Electrical, Radio and Machine Workers of America Local 1122 (NUGW-UE)
covers: Graduate students enrolled in Northwestern degree programs who provide instructional and research services for the University, including graduate assistants, teaching assistants, research assistants, and fellows. Article I excludes graduate students not providing instructional or research services; undergraduates; students not seeking Northwestern degrees, including visiting students; graders, tutors and proctors not otherwise providing instructional or research services; Assistant Chairs in residential colleges; Residential Assistants; students enrolled in the Pritzker School of Law; M.D.-seeking students in the Feinberg School of Medicine (including M.D./Ph.D. students in their M.D. phase); and students enrolled in the Medill School of Journalism.
note: First contract. Effective on ratification (March 15, 2024, per the University's CBA overview) through 11:59 p.m. on March 31, 2027. Article XXXI renews it for one-year periods unless either party gives written notice at least 60 days before March 31, that is, by about January 30, 2027 for the first renewal. The signature page (PDF page 36) is undated, so no signing date is given here. Rates are set in Appendix A; Article XXI applies them only while a graduate student works in a bargaining unit position. As of October 15, 2026, no successor bargaining had been announced; the union's home page shows a countdown to the March 31, 2027 expiration.

name: Northwestern University Graduate School (TGS) PhD funding
covers: Doctoral students funded through The Graduate School, typically for four quarters a year for at least five years
note: The Graduate School's published funding model and minimum annual stipend. Before the contract's June 1, 2024 rates, it was the only stated floor; since then the contract's TGS base stipend and the published minimum run side by side, the published figure a few dollars higher.

name: New York University and GSOC-UAW collective bargaining agreement, 2020-2026
union: Graduate Student Organizing Committee (GSOC), International Union, UAW, AFL-CIO and Local 2110, UAW (GSOC has been part of UAW Local 7902 since August 2025)
covers: Graduate students who teach classes (Ph.D. and Master's), graduate assistants, and research assistants employed by NYU, excluding among others graduate assistants at the School of Medicine, research assistants at Polytechnic Institute, and research assistants in the Biology, Chemistry, Neural Science, Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science and Psychology departments
note: The agreement ended August 31, 2026. GSOC's bargaining updates (latest October 7, 2026, after the 11th session) show a successor still being negotiated, with one article (Posting) tentatively agreed as of October 7, 2026; no cited source says the expired terms continue to apply. GSOC moved from UAW Local 2110 to UAW Local 7902 in August 2025.

name: GSAS Henry M. MacCracken Program (doctoral full-funding package)
covers: Most new doctoral students in the Graduate School of Arts and Science; not the GSAS affiliate programs in Basic Medical Sciences, Environmental Health Sciences, Cinema Studies, Performance Studies, Data Science, the Institute of Fine Arts, or the Institute for the Study of the Ancient World

name: Center for Data Science PhD fellowship
covers: PhD students in the Center for Data Science

name: Tandon School of Engineering Ph.D. student funding (SoE Fellowship and Research Assistantships)
covers: Ph.D. students at the Tandon School of Engineering

name: Steinhardt Fellowship Program and Research Assistantships for full-time PhD students
covers: Full-time PhD students in the Steinhardt School of Culture, Education, and Human Development

name: Stern School of Business PhD Program financial aid package
covers: Doctoral students in the Stern PhD Program

name: Vilcek Institute of Graduate Biomedical Sciences financial support for PhD candidates
covers: Graduate students and MD/PhD students at the Vilcek Institute, NYU Grossman School of Medicine

name: Penn State Table of Stipends for Graduate Assistants and Fox Graduate School graduate assistantship terms
covers: Graduate assistants (assistantships involving teaching, research, or administrative activities)
note: The stipend tables are published one academic year per page; the site lists 2023/2024 through 2026/2027, and every page shows "Last Revision: 06/24/2025". No union contract covers these graduate assistants yet (see history).

name: University of Pennsylvania and GETUP-UAW Local 5124 collective bargaining agreement
union: Graduate Workers Together at the University of Pennsylvania (GETUP-UAW Local 5124)
covers: All graduate and professional students who provide research or instructional services for the University, including Teaching Assistants, Teaching Fellows, Research Assistants, Research Fellows, Pre-Doctoral Trainees, and Student Workers, and Educational Fellowship Recipients who provide teaching or research services. Excludes professional students in the Veterinary, Dental, and Medical Schools (except qualifying joint-degree students), Educational Fellowship Recipients who provide no teaching or research services, and first-year Biology and first- and second-year Biomedical Graduate Studies PhD students in lab rotations.
note: The term runs from ratification to midnight on June 1, 2028 (Article 34); the union dates ratification to February 27, 2026. The signature page is undated. First contract; no successor exists or is due before 2028 (checked 2026-10-13).

name: University of Pennsylvania graduate stipend policy before the GETUP-UAW contract
covers: Ph.D. students (the University-wide minimum Ph.D. stipend; each school may pay more)
note: The University's minimum Ph.D. stipend, as stated on its graduate student support page (2025-26) and in its 2022-23 announcements (2023-24). The union calls it "Penn's previous policy", which the April 1, 2026 contract increases replaced.

name: Annenberg School for Communication PhD stipend and payroll funding, 2025-2026
covers: Doctoral students in the Annenberg School for Communication
note: Period is the payment schedule the sheet gives (August or September 2025 through August 2026). Replaced because the GETUP-UAW contract raised the minimum stipend to $49,000 from April 1, 2026, above this sheet's $44,027; the sheet itself says nothing of the contract.

name: Princeton University Graduate School University Rates for fellowship stipends and assistantship salaries
covers: Degree-seeking Ph.D. students on University fellowships, Teaching Assistantships, and Research Assistantships, and graduate students (including master's and DCE students) holding Teaching or Research Assistantships
note: Rates are published one academic year at a time; the live page shows 2026-27. The 2023-24 and 2024-25 tables name the assistantships "Assistantship in Instruction" and "Assistantship in Research"; from 2025-26 they are "Teaching Assistantship" and "Research Assistantship". No union contract covers Princeton graduate students, who rejected unionization in May 2024. The support overview also states that stipends have increased every year for more than two decades.

name: Purdue University graduate staff minimum salaries (Graduate Staff Employment Manual, Appendix B)
covers: Graduate staff appointments (Graduate Teaching Assistant, Graduate Research Assistant, Graduate Administrative/Professional, and Graduate Lecturer) on the West Lafayette, Fort Wayne, and Northwest campuses.
note: A university policy, not a collective bargaining agreement: none of the sources mentions a union or a bargaining agreement. The Graduate School issues the minimum salary scales annually; colleges may pay more. The February 2, 2026 manual still carries the 2025-26 table, and a search on 2026-10-14 found no 2026-27 table or announced change. In February 2025 the administration said it was reviewing a return to raising the minimum by the faculty and staff merit-pool percentage.

name: Rensselaer minimum graduate stipend, set each year by the Board of Trustees
covers: All graduate students receiving stipends from the Institute, from contracts/grants, and from Institute administered external sources
note: Published one academic year at a time on the Office of Graduate Education's Internal Funding page; the live page shows AY26-27. No graduate-worker union contract covers Rensselaer graduate students.

name: Rice University minimum Ph.D. stipend
covers: Ph.D. students enrolled in full-time study and in good standing, for the number of years in their original offer letter; the catalog applies the minimum to Rice fellows and to teaching and research assistants
note: The minimum took effect "Beginning July 1" in an announcement emailed November 23, 2022, so July 1, 2023; the 2022-23 catalog has no minimum and the 2023-24 catalog states $32,000. The catalog calls each year's figure the "current" minimum without dating it, so each rate is labeled with its catalog edition's academic year. No union contract covers Rice graduate students.

name: Rutgers and AAUP-AFT collective negotiations agreement, 2022-2026
union: Rutgers Council of AAUP Chapters, American Association of University Professors-American Federation of Teachers (AAUP-AFT)
covers: Rutgers University faculty members, teaching assistants and graduate assistants (plus legacy AAUP-BHSNJ unit members)
note: The agreement is dated as "made and entered into on this 8th day of May, 2023" (PDF page 6), but the signatures on PDF page 207 are undated, so no signing date is recorded. The union's FAQ states that the TA/GA article (Article 12) remains in effect until a successor is reached; it says nothing explicit about the salary article (Article 8.A), and no source found states the terms continue in general. Rutgers Business School's Ph.D. financial-assistance page gives the 2026-27 teaching assistant salary as $40,000, the agreement's FY2025-26 academic-year minimum, which indicates the salary minimums also stayed in place after June 30, 2026. As of the union's October 8, 2026 bargaining update, no tentative successor agreement had been announced.

name: Stanford University and UE Local 1043 (SGWU) collective bargaining agreement, 2024-2027
union: Stanford Graduate Workers Union (UE Local 1043)
covers: Ph.D., Master's (excluding MBA) and J.D. students who provide instructional or research services, including Teaching Assistants, Research Assistants, Course Assistants, and students on fellowship who provide instructional services
note: The first contract. It takes effect on ratification, which the union dates November 22, 2024, the same date Article 1 gives for the agreement, and renews for one-year periods after August 31, 2027 unless either side gives 60 days' notice of termination. The signatures, with e-signature stamps dated in January 2025, appear only as images. The 2024-25 rates take effect January 1, 2025; Autumn Quarter 2024 was paid at the university's earlier minimums plus a one-time supplement.

name: Stanford minimum assistantship salaries, 2023-24 (Graduate Financial Services)
covers: Research Assistants, Course Assistants, Teaching Assistants, Graduate Teaching Affiliates and Mentor Teaching Assistants in all schools
note: University-set minimums before the union contract, dated March 2023; replaced by the 2024-25 tables. The Autumn Quarter 2024 table repeats the same 50% figures.

name: Stanford minimum assistantship salaries, 2024-25 Autumn Quarter (Graduate Financial Services)
covers: Research Assistants, Course Assistants, Teaching Assistants, Graduate Teaching Affiliates and Mentor Teaching Assistants in all schools
note: The university-set minimums in force for Autumn Quarter 2024, before the first contract's rates. A new table effective January 1, 2025, issued pursuant to the agreement, replaced them for Winter, Spring and Summer Quarters.

name: Stanford 12-month 5-year funding commitment for PhD students
covers: Enrolled PhD and DMA students in good academic standing, for up to the first five years of the degree
note: Published in the Graduate Academic Policies and Procedures (GAP 7.1.1, last updated November 6, 2024), which funds students at the university's 20-hour-per-week Research Assistantship minimum; the provost's letter of November 25, 2024 confirms it to the union, which lists the letter among its contract documents. It is not an article of the collective bargaining agreement. The provost announced the commitment in July 2020, beginning with the 2020-21 academic year. The policy also covers DMA students, who are outside the bargaining unit. Status current on the GAP page as retrieved in October 2026.

name: Agreement between the State of New York and CWA Local 1104/Graduate Student Employees Union (Graduate Student Negotiating Unit)
union: Graduate Student Employees Union (GSEU), Communications Workers of America Local 1104

The mandate offered one-year bridge funding to units paying below the FY26 minimums, so no university floor applied before September 1, 2025.

name: Texas A&M Mandate for Payment of Tuition and Fees for PhD Graduate Assistants (GAT, GAR, GAL)
covers: Ph.D. students employed as Graduate Assistant-Teaching (GAT), Graduate Assistant-Research (GAR), and Graduate Assistant-Lecturer (GAL) at Texas A&M University and Texas A&M University at Galveston
note: A separate, older policy than the stipend minimums. Payment of resident tuition for Ph.D. graduate assistants dates from the major changes to the tuition payment mandate in January 2011 (FY12); the FY21 changes, recommended on December 2, 2019, added required university and college fees from Fall 2020 (FY21, which begins September 1, 2020). The Graduate and Professional School's current mandate page states the policy in force, with no end date.

name: Texas A&M graduate assistant benefits (non-resident tuition waiver and A&M System employee insurance)

The minimum-rates page summarizes them, and the HR graduate benefits page and the A&M System premium tables give the insurance terms.

name: University of Chicago and GSU-UE collective bargaining agreement
union: United Electrical, Radio and Machine Workers of America, UE Local 1103 (Graduate Students United, GSU-UE)
covers: Graduate students enrolled in University of Chicago degree programs who are employed to provide instructional or research services, including Teaching Assistants, Research Assistants, Graduate Student Lecturers, Instructional Graders, Preceptors, and Chicago Center for Teaching and Learning Teaching Fellows
note: The Provost's signature is dated 4/25/2024 and one union signature 4/23/24; the other union signature lines carry no date in the text layer. The agreement renews for one-year periods unless either party gives notice at least 60 days before March 31. Graduate Students United says it will negotiate a second contract at the start of 2027; no newer agreement had been reached by October 2026.

name: University of Chicago minimum PhD stipend before the GSU-UE agreement (2022-23, and 2023-24 as announced by the Provost on January 3, 2023)
covers: UChicago Ph.D. students

name: University of Massachusetts Amherst and GEO/UAW Local 2322 collective bargaining agreement, 2024-2027
union: Graduate Employee Organization (GEO), UAW Local 2322

note: The signature page dates the GEO and UAW signatures October 24-25, 2024 and the University's (Assistant Provost Mark Preble) October 28, 2024. Article 55 makes the agreement effective when signed by the University President, a signature the page does not show. If no successor is executed by August 31, 2027, the agreement stays in force until one is or an impasse is reached; negotiations may begin on or after February 1, 2027.

name: UMass Amherst campus minimum assistantship pay, as the Graduate School published it in 2023-24

The minimum then came from GEO's previous contract with the university; this records the minimum as the Graduate School's page stated it, and the earlier contract itself was not consulted. The 2024-2027 agreement (geo-2024) superseded it, first raising the minimum hourly rate 3% to $33.64, which is $32.66 times 1.03.

Maryland enacted collective bargaining rights for UMD graduate assistants in 2026 (HB 141, Chapter 774, approved by the Governor on May 26, 2026), effective July 1, 2028, so no bargaining agreement can exist before then.

name: Agreement between the Regents of the University of Michigan and the Graduate Employees' Organization
union: Graduate Employees' Organization (GEO), American Federation of Teachers, AFL-CIO Local 3550
covers: Graduate Student Instructors (GSIs) and Graduate Student Staff Assistants (GSSAs) on the Ann Arbor, Dearborn, and Flint campuses. Graduate Student Research Assistants (GSRAs) voted to join the bargaining unit in March 2026 but are not covered by this agreement's terms.
note: Dates from the cover page (August 25, 2023 - May 1, 2026). Article XXVI, Term of Agreement, says the agreement runs from ratification 'up to and including August 25, 2023', evidently a misprint for the end date, and that it was executed August 25, 2023; the signature page is dated August 28, 2023. Article XXVI also says that if no successor is negotiated by May 1, 2026, the agreement continues in full force unless either party gives 30 days' written notice of termination. As of 2026-10-13 no successor had been reached: bargaining began November 14, 2025, the university asked for state fact-finding in July 2026, and at the October 2, 2026 session GEO rejected the university's comprehensive package proposal (source hr-geo-negotiation-updates). Status is expired-continuing on Article XXVI's continuation clause together with the university's July and August 2026 statements calling the 2023-2026 agreement the current CBA; no source says either party gave notice of termination.

name: U-M minimum stipend rates for Graduate Student Research Assistants (Academic Human Resources)
covers: Graduate Student Research Assistants (GSRAs) on the Ann Arbor, Flint, and Dearborn campuses
note: No contract set GSRA pay through 2025-26: Academic Human Resources published the minimums in its annual memos, alongside the contractual GSI and GSSA rates. GSRAs voted to join GEO in March 2026 (election concluded March 26), and the 2026-27 memo says their rates are now subject to collective bargaining; the 2026-27 GSRA minimums are listed under this policy because the 2023-2026 agreement does not cover GSRAs. Status unknown: no source says whether these university-set minimums now count as a policy still in force or as the status quo pending a first contract covering GSRAs.

name: Rackham Graduate School 12-month funding model for Ph.D. students
covers: Rackham Ph.D. students on the Ann Arbor campus who are in good academic standing and within the funding period of their offer of admission. Doctor of Musical Arts students and Dearborn Ph.D. students are handled separately.
note: Announced by Rackham Dean Mike Solomon on March 24, 2023 and in effect from the spring/summer 2023 term; before it, Rackham's commitment covered only the fall and winter terms (eight months), a commitment dating from the 2010 continuous enrollment policy. It is a Rackham academic commitment, not part of the GEO agreement: the university's FAQ says Ph.D. funding outside GSI/GSSA employment is not subject to collective bargaining, and in the 2025-2026 bargaining GEO proposed extending the model to D.M.A. students. Programs meet it from fellowships, GSRA, and GSI/GSSA appointments, with a Rackham block-grant allocation filling gaps. Status current because Rackham's policy and funding pages, retrieved 2026-10-13, describe it as in force; no source gives an end date.

name: Collective Bargaining Agreement between the University of California and UAW Local 4811 (Academic Student Employees and Graduate Student Researchers, BX/BR)
union: International Union, United Automobile, Aerospace and Agricultural Implement Workers of America (UAW), Local 4811
covers: The unified Academic Student Employee unit (Teaching Assistants, Associate Instructors, Readers, Tutors) and Graduate Student Researchers, including GSR Trainees and Fellows, at all ten campuses and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory.
note: One agreement now covers both units, which had separate 2022 contracts. Article 40 makes it effective on ratification, which closed on March 20, 2026 (89.2% of the 15,976 ASE and GSR unit members voting were in favor). It runs to 11:59 p.m. on December 31, 2029, then year to year unless a party opens it by April 2029. Pay rises come from restructured salary tables rather than an across-the-board percentage, ending on a unified seven-point scale on October 1, 2029. UCSF Basic Sciences GSRs are placed at GSR salary point 6.

name: UT Austin student academic titles and pay rates (salary ranges set each fiscal year by the Office of the Executive Vice President and Provost)
covers: Students in academic titles, including Teaching Assistants, Assistant Instructors, and Graduate Research Assistants, university-wide

The university sets only a minimum-maximum range per title, and departments pay within it, so there is no single university-wide minimum: colleges set their own minimums or required rates above the floor (the College of Liberal Arts and College of Education minimums are recorded here; other colleges' minimums are not recorded). The live page gives 2026-2027; Wayback Machine snapshots give 2023-24 to 2025-26. Status current because the live page, updated 2026-08-25, gives the 2026-2027 fiscal year.

name: Virginia Tech graduate assistant compensation program (Board of Visitors-approved stipend table and Policy 6210)
covers: Graduate students on assistantship at Virginia Tech: Graduate Assistants (GA), Graduate Teaching Assistants (GTA), and Graduate Research Assistants (GRA)
note: No collective bargaining agreement covers Virginia Tech graduate assistants; pay is set by the Graduate School's stipend table, approved each year by the Board of Visitors as part of a graduate assistant compensation plan, and Policy 6210 requires every assistantship to pay a monthly stipend within that table. The table is a step scale of monthly ranges: 50 steps from 2022-23 to 2024-25, and Steps 0-11 from 2025-26. From 2023-24 the lowest steps are reserved for students whose stipend is combined with a supplemental fellowship, so the floor for an assistantship stipend alone is a higher step (Step 1 in 2022-23, Step 12 in 2023-24, Step 14 in 2024-25, Step 1 from 2025-26). Each table also prints 9-month and 12-month totals, and every rate includes an academic-year supplement, distributed over 18 pay periods, to offset comprehensive fees. Status is current because the 2026-27 table, effective August 10, 2026, is the latest published.

name: Collective Bargaining Agreement between Yale University and Local 33 UNITE HERE (2023-2028)
union: Local 33, UNITE HERE
covers: Students in the Graduate School of Arts and Sciences PhD and Master's programs (including PhD programs affiliated with a professional school) serving as Teaching Fellows, in other teaching job types (Grader, Discussion Section Leader, Lab Leader, Part-Time Acting Instructor, Teaching Assistant, Summer Assistant 1 and 2, Summer Session Instructor of Record), as Writing Fellows or Project Assistants, or as Primary and Secondary Research Assistants, including those on University Fellowship, training grants, and individual fellowships; and students in Yale's other professional degree programs, and non-degree students, in Teaching Fellow, other teaching, and Writing Fellow positions. Excluded are first-year Engineering and Applied Science (other than Computer Science) and Combined Program in Biology and Biomedical Sciences students appointed as Research Assistants, School of the Environment Research Assistants on University Fellowship (first-year students, and PhD students), Investigative Medicine RAs, and School of Management Teaching Assistants in courses shorter than a semester.
note: Article 1 says the agreement is entered into as of December 16, 2023, and Article 38 makes it effective upon ratification on that date. The signature page of this copy is blank, so no signing date is recorded. After July 31, 2028 it continues year to year unless either party gives notice; the parties are to begin negotiating a successor by January 31, 2028. No successor agreement was found as of 2026-10-13.

name: Yale Graduate School of Arts and Sciences financial aid policy (PhD stipend, tuition fellowship, and health award; Yale Health Basic Coverage for degree students)
covers: PhD students in the Graduate School of Arts and Sciences, generally during the years of support set out in the letter of admission; for Yale Health Basic Coverage, also GSAS master's students enrolled at least half-time
note: Living-expense support combines stipends with Teaching Fellow and Research Assistant pay, whose minimums the Local 33 agreement sets; the GSAS funding policy covers what the contract leaves out (tuition, fees, master's health coverage, and the length of support). Sources are the 2026-2027 GSAS bulletin and GSAS funding pages. Professional-school students in the bargaining unit are not covered by these GSAS pages.
